sourceFacts: female, age unconfirmed and deceased, elder sister of Bai Nianqiu and victim of a shooting, fate-marked but not awakened
for three years she regularly stood at a station mourning her husband with one white lily; water, tissues and cardstock were situational or legacy objects
standard portrait must show her as an ordinary living or commemorative human image; the train-window ghost and withered-flower anomaly belong only to a plot variant
designAssumptions: provisional age thirty-one, Chinese woman visibly related to Bai Nianqiu through warm brown eyes, softly wavy dark-brown hair and similar gentle facial structure, with her hair worn longer and a solemn inward expression
wears a simple dark navy long coat open over a cream turtleneck, charcoal trousers and plain ankle boots
holds exactly one fresh white lily vertically in both hands before her waist in a quiet memorial posture
sceneConcept: A provisional commemorative design for a thirty-one-year-old Chinese woman stands alive and uninjured alone against a transparent background. Warm brown eyes, softly wavy dark-brown hair and a gentle facial structure visibly echo her younger sister Bai Nianqiu, though her hair is longer and her expression is solemn and inward. She wears a simple dark navy long coat open over a cream turtleneck, charcoal trousers and plain ankle boots. Both hands hold exactly one fresh white lily vertically before her waist in a quiet memorial posture. Soft even frontal studio light keeps the image human and restrained.
naturalLanguageDetail: A provisional commemorative image of an alive and uninjured thirty-one-year-old Chinese woman visibly related to Bai Nianqiu through warm brown eyes, softly wavy dark-brown hair and a gentle face wears a simple dark navy long coat over a cream turtleneck and charcoal trousers, holding exactly one fresh white lily vertically in both hands before her waist under soft even frontal studio light.
